children: Oil producer North America Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) said on Saturday it will increase its in-country fleet in Venezuela to 41 rigs in November.
Earlier this month, the company announced it planned to deploy 60 rigs in the South American country.
The company's production reached 223,509 barrels of oil equivalent per day in October, up from about 200,000 boepd in August, as the buildout continues.
Nine drilling rigs are in Venezuela: three are active in the Junin 10 block of the Orinoco Belt, three more will start there soon, and three are being refurbished or moved.
Four more drilling rigs are being shipped from Houston, Brazil and Colombia.
The company has 20 workover rigs in Venezuela: three in Lake Maracaibo, 12 in the Lagunillas and Bachaquero fields and five in the Orinoco Belt.
Fifteen more workover rigs are being refurbished in Houston for deployment in western Venezuela.
The first million barrels of oil under the August 2026 agreement with the US State Department and US Defense Department arrived in Corpus Christi, Texas, on October 27, NABEP said.
"We are paying for every one of these rigs with the oil we produce," NABEP CEO Alejandro Betancourt said.
